# Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-312#speed-up-touch-review-checks

**Verdict: Caught.** With the file browser beside the code no longer bounded by the work area, a finger drag in the file browser moved the code pane together with the list (independently observed), and three of the four maintained touch review cases failed, both tablet cases among them. The catch is the helper expectation "the stroke's scrolling comes to rest" (`dashboard/tests/touchGestures.ts:115`), reached from `dashboard/tests/support/storyReviewTouchJourney.ts:201` in the tablet reading case and from `dashboard/tests/support/storyReviewTouchContext.ts:77` in the tablet context case. The claim is limited to those paths: the reading case's closing file-browser drag and its three assertions (`storyReviewTouchJourney.ts:215-218`) were never reached under this fault and are not shown to catch anything by this check.

**Next proof action (separate from the verdict).** None is needed for this fault: maintained proof already fails on it. What this check leaves unobserved is whether `storyReviewTouchJourney.ts:216-218` themselves fail first under any fault. Demonstrating that would take a different fault, one that leaves the file browser scrolling on its own and all earlier strokes working while the code also moves; that is a separate check, and whether it is worth running is the caller's decision.

## Story, revision and promise

- Story: `SEED-312#speed-up-touch-review-checks`, `.planning/seeds/SEED-312-touch-review-checks.md`, section "Speed up touch review checks". Plan read for context only: `.planning/slice-plans/592-speed-up-touch-review-checks/PLAN.md`.
- Revision checked: `b9d7cb61a5c11226bbfa9e0f1d3112aebd5d85fc`, in a detached scratch worktree of repository `/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough`.
- Promise (Key examples): "Reading on a tablet. With the file browser beside the code, the same drags give the same independent result in each pane.", together with the phone example's "A drag in the file browser then moves the list and leaves the code where it was." Scope gives the tablet this repetition because its arrangement changes it: "the file browser above the code in a narrow review or beside it in a wide one".
- Expected observable behavior: at tablet portrait (768 x 1024) a finger drag in the file browser changes the file browser's own scroll position and leaves the code pane, the diff heading and the fixed top where they were.

## Fault

- Location and change: `dashboard/src/story-review.css`, rule `.story-review-files`, one added declaration `align-self: flex-start;` (a plausible cosmetic edit: let the browser's frame end with its list). Fixtures and assertions were left intact.
- Effect: in the side-by-side arrangement the file browser takes its content height, overflows the work area, and the review body becomes the one scroller for both panes. In the stacked arrangement `max-height: 40%` still bounds it, so the fault is specific to the file browser sitting beside the code.
- Not a repeat of execution's faults: F2 (`overflow: visible`, no `min-height`) broke every arrangement and failed all four cases at "room for an in-view finger stroke"; F4 is the diff's `min-width`. No recorded fault removed the file browser's independence only where it sits beside the code.

## Hints validated, and what changed

- Promise, focused command and fixture were reused unchanged: `npm run --silent test:dashboard -- tests/review/story-review-touch.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list` from the checkout root, with the comparison `openReviewByTouch` arranges.
- Fault: I used the hint's second suggestion (the two panes sharing one scroller in the wide arrangement). I did not use scroll chaining from the file browser into the code pane: the panes are siblings, so native chaining can only reach their shared ancestor; making the list scroll on its own while the code also moves would need an invented script coupling, which I judged not plausible as a regression.
- Assertion, consequential change: the hinted assertions at `storyReviewTouchJourney.ts:215-218` are valid at this revision but were not what caught the fault. Once the body is the shared scroller, choosing the long file scrolls the body, the code pane's top goes beneath the fixed top, and the reading case stops at its earlier return stroke (`:201`). I report the assertion that actually failed.

## Maintained checks examined

`dashboard/tests/review/story-review-touch.spec.ts`, all four cases, one worker:

| Case | Baseline | Faulted | Restored |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| phone › chooses a comparison and file and reads within each pane | pass 18.5 s | pass 25.4 s | pass 14.1 s |
| phone › keeps the chosen file and reading places through rotation and panel controls | pass 13.7 s | FAIL 8.6 s | pass 13.5 s |
| tablet › chooses a comparison and file and reads within each pane | pass 8.9 s | FAIL 12.9 s | pass 6.4 s |
| tablet › keeps the chosen file and reading places through rotation and panel controls | pass 8.5 s | FAIL 12.7 s | pass 5.7 s |

Faulted failures, all by an expectation and none by a test timeout (each case ended in under 13 s against 30 s and 60 s budgets):

- Tablet reading: `Error: the stroke's scrolling comes to rest`, "Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate", `touchGestures.ts:115`, called from `storyReviewTouchJourney.ts:201` (the one stroke back in the code pane, `scrollByTouch(page, code, back, "vertical", undefined, code)`).
- Tablet context: the same expectation at `touchGestures.ts:115`, called from `storyReviewTouchContext.ts:77` (`scrollByTouch(page, browser, 100, "vertical", undefined, browser)`), which is this journey's own finger drag in the file browser beside the code.
- Phone context: `storyReviewTouchContext.ts:52` in `expectKept`, called at `:91` after the first rotation, "Expected: 625 Received: 0" for the file browser's place.
- Phone reading passed, as a fault confined to the side-by-side arrangement should leave it.

## Run observations

Environment: Node 24.21.0, Homebrew Bash first on `PATH`, `caffeinate -s -i`, `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` unset. One-minute load between 13 and 34 across the runs. Scratch setup `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`, `browser`, `check` each exited 0.

- **Baseline.** 4 passed (57.6 s), exit 0, before any edit. Pre-probe state recorded: `HEAD` `b9d7cb61a`, `git status --porcelain` empty, empty diff.
- **Reach.** A scratch witness spec (not maintained proof; tablet portrait, touch, the journey's own `openReviewByTouch` and `selectAddedFileByTouch`) read the built page in both states. Faulted: computed `align-self` of `.story-review-files` is `flex-start`, work area direction `row`, file browser `clientHeight` 936 = `scrollHeight` 936 (was 691 of 936), body `scrollHeight` 950 against `clientHeight` 721 (was 721 of 721). The dashboard build is made per run, so the edit was in the served page.
- **Wrong behavior, independently observed.** After the long file is chosen the body is scrolled 229 px (unfaulted 0): the diff heading sits at y 86 and the code pane's top at y 130, beneath the fixed top that spans y 79-303 (unfaulted: heading 315, code 359). A native finger drag of 100 px starting at (157, 327), a shown point inside the file browser (`elementFromPoint` inside `.story-review-files`), gave:
  - faulted: file browser `scrollTop` 0 → 0, body `scrollTop` 229 → 144, code pane box y 130.1 → 215.1, diff heading y 86.1 → 171.1, first code line y 150.8 → 235.8, chosen row y 876.5 → 961.5. The code moved 85 px with the list; code `scrollTop` stayed 0.
  - unfaulted, same stroke: file browser `scrollTop` 245 → 160, body 0 → 0, code pane box, diff heading and first code line unchanged.
- **Why the maintained strokes fail (path of the catch).** The witness also ran the helper's own call `scrollByTouch(page, browser, 100)` in the faulted layout: its finger starts 8 px inside the browser's box, at (157, 94), where `elementFromPoint` is a label inside `.story-review-top`; nothing moved (file browser 0, body 229, code box unchanged). Unfaulted, the same call starts inside the file browser and moves it 245 → 160. That is the tablet context case's stroke at `:77`: the file browser never scrolls, so its `scrollend` never arrives. For the tablet reading case's stroke at `:201` the start point is derived, not separately witnessed: the helper starts 8 px below the code pane's top, y 138 by the measured box, inside the fixed top's measured span.
- **Not independently observed.** The phone context failure's mechanism. Its message (the browser's place 625 → 0 after rotating to landscape) is consistent with the phone's landscape review also placing the browser beside the code, but I did not measure that arrangement.
- **Restoration.** The fault was applied from a saved patch and reversed by a shell exit trap around the faulted runs ("fault reversed by trap"). The witness spec was deleted. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` matched the pre-probe record (empty), the diff hash matched the empty pre-probe diff, `HEAD` was unchanged, and `align-self` no longer appears in `dashboard/src/story-review.css`. The same command then gave 4 passed (42.1 s), exit 0. Only the ignored `dashboard/test-results/` of the failed run remained, and it went with the checkout: the scratch worktree was removed with `git worktree remove --force` and is no longer registered. No path in the story's worktree or any other existing worktree was edited, and the stash was not used.

Evidence files, all under `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/cb428881/tmp/intent-coverage/`: `baseline-1.log`, `faulted-1.log`, `restored-1.log`, `witness-unfaulted.log`, `witness-faulted.log`, `witness.jsonl` (the measurements above), `witness.spec.ts.txt` (the scratch witness), `fault.patch`, `pre-probe-*.txt`, `post-probe-status.txt`, `setup-*.log`.

## Prior disposition the evidence matches

The catch arrives as the generic "the stroke's scrolling comes to rest" after a 5 s poll, not as a named reading expectation. The plan already records this shape as G6 ("A pane that barely moves fails the return stroke at scrollend, not at a reading expectation"), disposed as proved because the story asks only that the fault fail a remaining case. This check recognizes that recorded disposition on a new fault; it makes no new repair decision, and test repair and follow-up routing stay with the caller.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** 234 s of whole-command wall time (measured, shell clock around each command) over five Playwright commands: baseline 59 s, unfaulted witness 29 s, faulted maintained 69 s, faulted witness 34 s, restored 43 s. The runner's own totals were 57.6 s, 27.8 s, 1.1 min, 32.2 s and 42.1 s. The three scratch setup stages were not timed separately.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no person took part in this invocation and no separate measure of human time was recorded.
- **Agent effort.** About 30 tool operations by one agent (estimated, counted from this run's own steps). Token and compute figures are unavailable: this agent has no meter for them.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 684137 ms (measured), from 1794418288000 to 1794418972137 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

---

## Wrap-up disposition (Story Wrap Up, 2026-11-12)

- Checked revision: `b9d7cb61a5c11226bbfa9e0f1d3112aebd5d85fc` of SEED-312#speed-up-touch-review-checks. One probe; it does not protect the whole story.
- Evidence: the report above. With the file browser beside the code no longer bounded by the work area, three of the four touch review cases failed by an expectation, both tablet cases among them; restoration was verified and the restored run passed 4 of 4.
- Decision: no follow-up. The verdict is Caught and names no actionable gap. The report's note that the reading case's closing file-browser assertions were not the ones that failed describes this fault's path, with no wrong behavior observed passing them; the same shape was already accepted during execution, where the story asks that such a fault fail a remaining case.
- Canonical follow-up links: none.
